english.title: Dog owner / person in charge not cause collar to be worn
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the

(A)_[owner]_
(B)_[person in charge]_

of a dog, without lawful authority or excuse, caused the dog to be in a

(C)_[highway namely **(..SPECIFY HIGHWAY..)]_
(D)_[place of public resort, namely **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..)]_

whilst it was not wearing a collar with the name and address of the owner inscribed thereon or on a plate or badge attached to it
english.legislation: Contrary to article 3 of the Control of Dogs Order 1992, and sections 72 and 75 of the Animal Health Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being the owner/person in charge of dog
without lawful authority/excuse
cause the dog to be in highway/place of public resort
while not wearing collar bearing name and address of owner

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Enforcement of this legislation is the responsibility of local authority officers, and NOT the police.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
